note: Every number of the cloud deck. Units are camera heights at the fit of frame 3150 (1 unit = 0.1725 degrees on the sphere). The chart has its origin under the storm, y along the view on the ground, x to the right. maps: the height maps from the finest to the widest, centre and size in units, pixels per side (the web set holds half).

tool.note: Numbers of the tools in assets-src/jupiter/deck that lay the canvas back onto the sphere. heightGain: gain of the depth tool's relief (deck/relief.py), fitted so the storm's walls stand as in the image. reliefSigmaPx: the relief is the depth tool's range over the smooth sphere's range, less its own mean over this many canvas pixels. reliefReach: the relief fades with the range, gone at this many units. depthBlurPx: blur of the image heights in canvas pixels (a map may name its own). resolveFactor, minResolve: the scale the image resolves on the ground is its footprint along the view times resolveFactor, at least minResolve units. trustFrom, trustTo: the image's heights are used where that scale is under trustFrom and not at all over trustTo. heightBlur: least blur of the heights in units (a map may name its own: the fore map holds the ground under the flight at the scale the canvas resolves there, so a crest of the heights stands where the canvas shows it). trustFeather: blur of that trust in units. slopeMax: no stored height may rise faster than this over the ground (a cone is laid over every top and the higher of the two kept), so the march, which sizes a step by the height over the ground and this slope, cannot step over a wall. heightRange: the lowest and highest height the maps store. reliefFade: the heights go to zero from reliefFade[0] to reliefFade[1] units from the point under the fit camera. plateRelief, plateReliefScale: where the image's heights are not used the near map takes the depth tool's relief of the top down near plate, with this gain, less its own mean over plateReliefScale units. roughBand, roughSpread, roughLevel: a plate's alpha is its own roughness, the energy between the scales roughBand in units, spread over roughSpread units, 1 at roughLevel.

canvas.note: The picture the fields are laid back from: the wide canvas of the earlier build (the approved close image in the middle, aprons at the same scale on all sides, recipe in RECIPE.md), with the approved image itself pasted over the middle. scale: canvas size over the size of the approved image. feather: image pixels from the border of the approved image over which the paste fades in. depthShrink: the depth tool runs on the canvas shrunk by this.

core.note: Inside the approved image the fields take their colour from the core: the approved image at scale times its size (the upscale tool, then the fine fold detail of the earlier build, recipe in RECIPE.md under the terrain deck, steps 2 and 11). lockPx: above this many core pixels the core is held to the tone of the approved image. feather: image pixels from the border of the approved image over which the core fades in.

light.note: azimuthDeg: the direction to the Sun on the ground of the chart, measured from the chart's x axis toward its y axis, as the approved image shows it. The function detail is embossed along it and the air is measured about it.

look.note: Numbers of the shader in clouds.ts. shell: lowest and highest height of the layer the march runs in. march: slack added to the slope of the ray when a step is sized by the height over the ground, least step in pixel footprints, a hit counts under this many footprints, most steps. detail: the function detail is a field of rounded tops made per wave length (cells with one seeded top each, each wave turned against the last): the largest wave in units, how much a top is brighter than the crease beside it, a wave may be this many pixels of the canvas at most (the scale the laid back image resolves at that spot, the mean of across and along its view), and this many pixel footprints at least. detailLook: the height a top stands over the mean, power by which a wave's slope falls with its length, least roughness, most change of brightness. detailTone: how much a slope toward the Sun's azimuth lights a top. foot: least cosine between ray and ground in the footprint, the footprint is cut into taps when it is longer than this times its width, most taps. blend: share of a height map's half width where it starts to give way to the next and where it ends. join: the same for the plates. trust: the image field is shown fully while the smear of a texel across the footprint of a 1080th of the frame height (a pixel of the 16 by 9 master, whatever the format) is under trust[0] such footprints and not at all over trust[1]; trust[2] = 1 takes the image field away (a check of the plates alone). The two numbers are set so wide that the image field is never given up by the angle of view: the ground it covers has one look from every side, and what the angle shows is its own paint laid flat. stretch: a texel may be enlarged this many times before the lookup is widened, most change of tone the plates' own detail may add to a widened lookup (1 = none), most widening, least sine between the fit camera's ray and the ground. anisotropy: taps of the texture filter.

air.note: The air between the camera and the deck, measured by deck/air.py on the approved view: for the plates, which hold the deck as it is from straight above, it gives the share of their light that comes through (by the sine of the angle between the ray and the ground) and the light the air adds (by that sine and by the turn of the ray away from the Sun's azimuth, mirrored). sinRange: the sines of the first and last knot, spaced by ratio. knots: count over the sine, count over the turn from 0 to 180 degrees. clear: between these sines the air ends, so a steep ray sees the plates as they are. minTexels: texels of the view chart a cell needs. smooth: blur of the added light in cells. The weight by which the air is gone is not kept here: it is read from the place on the ground (place.json scene.air), the same at every height of the camera, so the ground the approved view saw keeps the air it was painted in from the first frame of the dive and nothing comes in as the camera sinks. assets-src/jupiter/deck/lift.py and lift-measure.json are the history of the weight solved by film time (the largest level step was 4.84 a frame then).

flight.note: The flight of the surface view: one flight that takes the dive's motion at its first frame and hands the rise its motion at its last. seconds: its length. The camera passes the pose of the approved image at the middle. Up to the middle the forward speed over the ground goes from startUnitsPerSecond with the power of the elapsed share (endUnitsPerSecond is what that law would reach at the end), and the camera comes down: startAbove units higher at the start, falling with the sinkPower of the share of the way still to go, so it stays near the bottom plane of the approved view and little ground shows that the image never saw. bend: from the end of the judged middle frame's own shutter the push bends into a track across and on into a pull back up the lens's own line, which is the line the rise leaves along. The heading of the flight turns from straight ahead to straight back along the lens, through the right where through is -1 and through the left where it is 1 (to the right the eye stays over ground the approved image saw until the rise has lifted it; to the left the frame's bottom left corner left that ground four frames after the seam, while the eye was still low), on a smooth step that has no turn at either end, and the climb comes in with that step raised to climbPower, so the track across stays level and the camera lifts only as it pulls back. The speed over the camera's own height rises in a straight line from what the middle frame has to endPerSecond, so it never falls. The way is summed once in steps of 1 over stepsPerSecond and read between them through a cubic with the true speeds, so it holds at any fraction of a frame; beyondSeconds is how far past the seam the table reaches, straight on. ease: units and unitsPerSecond are the old cut of the way; they act only inside the shutter of the judged middle frame, so that frame's camera stays what it was to the byte.

view.note: The image field: the canvas laid onto the heights in a chart that matches the view of the fit camera (deck/view.py), so no texel is stretched at the fit pose. Since the fit camera looks its own picture up (image), the chart is seen only where that camera saw nothing or saw the ground too steeply; what it holds there is made by the fill below. thetaDeg: the chart's span of azimuth about the point under the fit camera, from the chart's y axis toward x. psiNearDeg: its nearest ground as the angle of the ray under the horizon. horizonMargin: units of ground distance left out before the horizon. pixels: the size of the chart the geometry is worked out on. fine: the stored chart holds this many texels per such pixel each way. imageMargin: canvas pixels at the canvas border that are not used. Ground the fit camera did not see is found per stored texel by the same test the shader uses (image.hidden against the stored range), so chart and shader agree to the texel. steep: ground whose texel is over this many times longer than on level ground counts as unseen too. Both are filled along the view: the colour of the ground just beyond the gap's far border (the mean of fillMean pixels) runs into the gap and passes to the colour just before its near border, which leaves out hiddenSkip pixels, so a narrow gap is never darker or lighter than both its sides. fillEdge: the outline of the steep ground is smoothed by this many pixels before it is laid on the fine grid. fillSmooth: the distances to the two borders are averaged across the view over this many pixels. fillNear: the ground before the gap (the crest that hides it) is mirrored in only over the last part of the way from the far border to the near one, from this share on; before it the gap holds the far ground alone, which is what a camera ahead of the fit pose sees first. fillAcross: the two border colours are averaged across the view over fillAcross[0] pixels at the border and over fillAcross[1] pixels from fillAcross[2] pixels into the gap on, so a wide gap carries no stripes. fillDetail: the fine structure (what is left of the canvas after a blur of fillDetail[3] pixels) of the ground mirrored about the two borders is added fillDetail[0] times, from fillDetail[1] to fillDetail[2] pixels inside the gap on; nearer to a border the gap is the plain run of colour. fillLength: a filled texel is stored this many times the gap's width longer than level ground where it holds no fine structure, so the shader's own detail fills it at the scale of the pixel. lengthRange: the shortest and longest ground length of a texel the alpha channel stores, by ratio. fade: canvas pixels from the canvas border between which the image field fades out.

limb.note: Glow over the limb as a table over (sunward place of the limb point, tangent height). deck/limb.py measures it on the approved image: python3 limb.py clear, render frame 3150 at the draft tier, python3 limb.py RENDER.png. cover = tangent heights between which the glow stops hiding the sky patch. Rows are spaced by the square root of the height.

plates.note: Top down plates of the place, made from the approved close image by assets-src/jupiter/plates (recipe in assets-src/jupiter/RECIPE.md). Units and chart as the maps; size and pixels are x then y. They hold albedo in the globe's coding (values above white kept), so the globe shows them as the deepest levels of its patches. order: the order in which the plates are made. parents: the plate a canvas is enlarged from; without one the canvas starts from the globe's own albedo at the place, with the flow frozen as in place.json (globeBlurPx: how soft that is in plate pixels). inset: a finished finer plate laid into the canvas at its own place. grade: one colour, the median over the laid back image within gradeRadius units of the vortex of the close image over the globe's albedo, both at a scale of gradeScale units. The plates were made as the close image divided by it. Since round 2 of the second note no program reads it: the plates hold the close image's light, and the globe and the deck both draw them over place.json solved.light, the globe's own light on a ground that faces the Sun at the place, with no exposure by height or time. useBlur: the laid back image is used where its own blur along the view is under useBlur[0] units, and not at all over useBlur[1]; beyond, near the image's horizon, the globe's own structure stays. flatten: from flatten[0] to flatten[1] units of ground distance from the close camera the laid back image gives up its tone above a scale of flatten[2] units to the globe's, because there its tone is the haze of a low view, not the cloud. carry: outside the laid back image the canvas carries the image's tone on from the border (measured at a scale of carry[0] units) and lets it go over carry[1] units. free: outside the laid back image the repaint is tied to the canvas at a scale that grows by this many pixels of blur per pixel of distance from the border. softPx: plate pixels of blur per unit of the image's own blur along the view, which marks unresolved parts as unfinished for the repaint. parentBlurPx: the blur of a level enlarged from the level above. clear: the globe's own structure is taken away within clear[0] units of the vortex (fading out to clear[1]) by a blur of clear[2] units, so the repaint closes the storm of the close image all the way round and the globe's small oval, which is that storm seen from far, does not stand beside it. bandPx: width and blur, in plate pixels, of the unfinished band along the border of the laid back image. finishedPx: blur under which the canvas is kept as it is. lock: the repaint keeps its own structure below lock[0] times the canvas blur (at least lock[1], at most lock[2] pixels) and takes the canvas above. lockGain: strength of the repaint's own structure. hiddenError: fixed point error of the lay back, in units, over which a place counts as hidden from the close image. feather: width of the join in units. nest: the near plate keeps its own repaint inside nest[0] units from its centre and is the mid plate beyond nest[1], measured with the power norm nestPower (a rounded square); the mid plate is the near plate made smaller inside the same shape. upward: assets-src/jupiter/plates/upward.py takes the place as the plates show it from above (fore, near and mid plate nested as the globe nests them) and writes it, reduced by area to the texel of a level above the mid plate, into the levels named in levels: far is the far plate (in the plates' coding), wrap is the globe's wrap and patches are its three patches (there divided by the grade, times the tone and calm fields, as the globe shows the plates). All three are written: the globe carries the place from the hold down (one Jupiter outranks the bytes of the hold inside a small disc round the place), so no height brings the storm in. from: the commit whose wrap and patches carry no place; the tool starts from those on every run, so a second run writes the same bytes. border: full within the first distance in units from the vortex, none from the second. spread: the point spread, in units of the chart, through which the place is written into each level of the globe's own imagery (a Gaussian of that width, in linear light, after the reduction by area). Each level is a picture of the planet with a point spread of its own, and nothing written into it may be crisper than the picture is: assets-src/jupiter/plates/spread.py measures it on the level as it stood before the place was written (the sharpest tenth of its clean edges, the fiftieth of its texels with the steepest gradient whose profile rises without a turn over 6 texels to either side): 1.30 texels of the wrap, 1.10, 1.20 and 1.02 texels of the three patches, in the full set; the web set takes the same widths in units and is only softer. For the wrap the octaves say the same: unfiltered, the place held 7.92 and 6.53 levels (rms of luma) in its two finest octaves where the great red storm of the same picture holds 4.26 and 4.05; through 1.25 texels it holds 2.43 and 3.99 (review of round 2, condition b of 23:34: in the hold nothing in the place is crisper than the hero's own detail round it). marginDeg: how far past the border the tool looks for texels.

move.note: The place stands on a storm the globe shows from orbit: the eye of the pale spiral oval east of the great red storm, where the globe's Sun stands as low as the close image shows it (place.json oval). assets-src/jupiter/plates/move.py lays the plates that reach beyond the painted storm on that ground: the globe's own imagery there with the flow at rest (softened as globeSoftenPx says) times the globe's light at the place (place.json solved.light). plates: the plates it writes. keep: per plate, the radius in units round the vortex inside which the painted plate stays as it was baked (read from the commit named in from) and the radius from which the plate is the globe's ground alone; between the two they blend smoothly. So the painted storm is the eye of the globe's own oval and the oval's spiral arms run round it. shade: see its own note. After it run plates/tone.py, plates/calm.py and plates/upward.py, which writes the storm into the far plate and into the globe's own imagery (upward: levels and border), so that the globe carries the place from the hold down and no height brings it in.

shade.note: The storm keeps its own shade past the painted disc: the tone of the kept paint against the hero ground in a ring just inside the border, by direction about the vortex, is carried onto the hero ground beyond the border and let go between the two radii of reach, in units from the vortex. Only shade, never a lift. So the dark side of the storm ends as a soft shadow on the oval and not as a cut edge, at every height alike.

image.note: The fit camera looks its own picture up: a point of the deck that the fit camera saw takes its colour from the canvas at the pixel where that camera saw it (deck/image.py writes the canvas, the core at twice its scale for the approved image, and the range the fit camera saw along every ray), so the frame at the fit pose is the approved image, and from any other pose every point keeps the colour it had. A point the fit camera did not see (farther along its ray than the stored range) takes the fill of the view chart. rangeShrink: canvas pixels per stored range, for the full and the web set. rangeLog2: the least and the greatest stored range as powers of two. hidden: a point counts as seen while it lies less than hidden[0] of the stored range beyond it, and as unseen from hidden[1]. sharpen: the footprint of a lookup in the canvas is taken this many times its true size. quality: of the stored pictures. march: slack, least step and hit distance in stored pixels, most steps, of the tool march. reach: units from the point under the fit camera beyond which the deck is the smooth sphere. steep: a point the fit camera saw so steeply that one pixel of the canvas is drawn over more than steep[0] 1080ths of the frame height (pixels of the 16 by 9 master, whatever the format) passes to the fill of the view chart, fully from steep[1] on; below that the canvas is shown as it is and the shader's own detail fills the scale it lacks.

tone.note: The tone of the approved view as a smooth field over the ground, written by assets-src/jupiter/plates/tone.py to deck-tone.bin (three stacked blocks of pixels x pixels, 16 bit, value times scale): the approved view laid on the ground over the plates, both blurred by blurUnits, carried out smoothly past the ground the view saw, and led back to 1 between the fade distances from the point under its camera. The plates are multiplied by it at every height of the camera and by both programs, so the ground the view saw and the ground beside it have one tone from above. Up to round 46 the tone came in with the height of the camera (lift), and with it a second limb and a bank of pale cloud faded in place on the way down and up; that weight is gone. known: the view counts fully within the first distance in units from the point under its camera and not past the second. The same two distances end the approved view itself where the deck draws it, so its footprint on the ground has a soft round edge that is the same from every height. imageBlurPx: blur of the view before it is laid down. marginPx: rim of the canvas left out. range: least and most ratio.

calm.note: A second smooth field over the ground, written by assets-src/jupiter/plates/calm.py to deck-calm.bin (three stacked blocks of pixels x pixels, 16 bit, value times scale; pixels must equal tone.pixels, because the loader lays it beside the tone field in one texture). The ground is multiplied by it wherever it is multiplied by the tone field: the plates at every height of the camera, by both programs, and not the approved view itself. It changes two things the plates paint east of the storm, which from above read as faults. hue: where the ground outside the near plate's own repaint is colder than its surround, it is led to the hue of the warm ground around it. The measure is (blue - red) / (blue + red) of the ground blurred by blurUnits; the first number of cold is none and the second is full, the same way round for warm; darkBias weights a second blur towards the dark, so bright cloud tops inside a cold area do not hide it. The warm ground is carried in over surroundUnits; the target is at least lift times its brightness. The gain of a channel is at most the number most, all three channels scaled together so the hue holds, and at least the number least. softUnits blurs the mask and the gain. nestShare is the share of the near plate's own repaint above which hue does nothing. shade: the storm's cast shade in the near plate ends at the straight line where that plate gives way to the globe's own picture (plates.nest). The shade is carried on past that line: the ground outside is darkened to the level carried out from inside (carryUnits; inside is where the repaint's share is over the number inside, the ground outside is measured where it is under the number outside), fully up to the first distance of reach from the storm's centre and not at all from the second, that distance moved by a seeded value noise (noise: wavelength and amplitude in units; seed), and only where the inside is darker than the outside by the ratios in dark (none at the first, full at the second) and between the rows (chart y: off, on, on, off). lift: inside, the shade is lifted by up to the third number, rising from the first to the second distance from the storm's centre, so the step into the carried shade is small. edgeUnits: the field is led back to 1 over this distance inside its own border. preview: zoom and exposure of the before and after picture the script writes to out/work/jupiter/calm.

above.note: How the ground looks from above the air, so the far field of the surface view's scene is the globe's far field at the handover. Knots lie evenly in the square root of the sine of the angle between the ray and the ground (0 at the horizon, 1 straight down). gain: the light of the ground is multiplied by it. air: light added on top, in the scene's own units before the exposure. Both act by the weight by which the air is gone (place.json scene.air, read from the place on the ground). Every gain is 1 and all added light is 0 today, so the tables change no pixel. Measured at frame 3024 on stills of both sides: the globe alone (beauty/side=orbit/noplace) over the scene, medians per bin of the sine; under a sine of 0.2 the spread of the globe no longer follows the scene, so there the rest is added light.
above.evenNote: even: the share of the mix between the look under the air and the look from above that is taken in the logarithm of the light (1: the same ratio of light for the same step of the weight, so the far ground does not turn pale in the lowest tenth of the weight; 0: the straight mix). At a weight of 0 and of 1 the picture is the same either way. floor: the least light that enters the logarithm.

life.note: What moves in the surface view while the camera flies (mail 230). Every motion is a rigid turn or a rigid drift of a function of the ground point, set by time alone; no field is dragged through a flow and no picture is scrolled. storm: the vortex turns about centre (chart units, the middle of the red disc on the near plate) as a rigid body inside coreUnits, less and less out to rimUnits, where the ground stands still. Heights, colours, the image lookup and the function detail all read the same turned ground point, so the relief turns with its colour. The turn is boundDeg times tanh(degPerSecond times seconds from the middle of the surface view over boundDeg): degPerSecond counter clockwise seen from above at the middle (frame 3150, where the turn is zero and the picture is the approved one), never more than boundDeg either way. Wind up: in the 180 frames the rim of the core turns 7.62 degrees either way, spread over the 3.4 units from core to rim; the largest shear of the approved shapes there is 0.13 either way. The globe draws the plates of the place with the same turn, so both sides of a handover agree. rings: each ring adds its own turn to everything inside the inner one of its two edgeUnits, falling to nothing by a smoothstep at the outer one, in the same bounded form (boundDeg times tanh(degPerSecond times seconds over boundDeg)). There is one ring, and it takes the storm's turn back: the ground within 0.9 units of the centre, the red eye and its walls, stands still and keeps its shape, and the clouds run round it. Between 0.9 and 1.6 units the turn comes in (the shear there is 0.24 at the two ends of the surface view and none at the middle); from 1.6 units out the storm turns as written above. Up to round 46 four rings outran one another inside the core (10, 8, 6 and 4 degrees a second) and sheared the eye to nearly twice its width over its height by frame 3239. eddies: small vortices of the picture turn about their own centres (chart units as stored, carried round by the storm) in the same form: rigid inside coreUnits, still at rimUnits, degPerSecond at the middle (negative is clockwise), never more than boundDeg; in the 180 frames 6.34 degrees either way, the rim four cores out, largest shear 0.14. haze: two thin rigid sheets of cloud at heightUnits over the datum (both above the relief, which stays within about 0.1), one on each side of the storm (side -1 south, 1 north of the line through the storm centre along the jet; a sheet begins between its two edgeUnits from that line and ends between its two reachUnits from the centre), drifting along the jet at unitsPerSecond (east is positive; the two go opposite ways, as the jets on the two sides of an anticyclone do). The density of a sheet is a function of its own point: banks (bankUnits, warp) made of fibres along the jet (fibreUnits, fibreOctaves, fibreShare, fibreWarp), value noise in octaves (lacunarity, octaveGain, octaveShift, warpSeed, octaveFade by the pixel footprint), cover the two thresholds, footprint the fade where a 1080th of the frame height (a pixel of the 16 by 9 master, whatever the format) is wider than the fibres. A sheet lightens what lies behind it by depth over the cosine of the view (at least minCosine) with the low passed colour of its ground (lightBlurUnits) times glow, so it takes the tone of its ground; that light is weighted by forward [g, gain] as min(gain x ((1 - g) / sqrt(1 + g x g - 2 g c))^3, 1), c being the cosine between the view ray and the direction to the Sun, so thin cloud shows where one looks toward the Sun and nearly vanishes where one looks down on it (measured: without the weight the south sheet lay as a pale mist band over the foreground at 3060 to 3135); on the deck it lays a shadow of shadowDepth where the Sun's ray (sunElevationDeg) passes through it, tinted by shadowTint, displaced by the height between sheet and ground, fading over softUnits where the ground reaches the sheet. Both count only where the ground is sunlit (lit: thresholds on the warmth of the low passed ground). flash: lightning inside the dark blue cloud. At each site (at in chart units as stored, radiusUnits) an envelope e = sum of strength x u x exp(1 - u) runs, u being the time since an event over riseSeconds. Two things follow from it. The cold pixels (cold: thresholds on blue against red, the sum of the two never taken below core.floor so that the black of the plate does not switch the mask; bright: thresholds on luminance, darker pixels take the share surround) are multiplied by exp(gain x e x exp(-q)), q being the squared distance over radiusUnits squared. And light is added: glow x e x (exp(-q x core.tight) + core.spill x exp(-q)) x the square root of the luminance of the pixel, a small bright heart with a wide faint spill that keeps the forms of the cloud it lights. The events [seconds from the middle, strength] were drawn once from seed and are listed, so the light is a function of time alone; a glow needs riseSeconds (about 4 frames) to its peak and fades over about 20, so nothing strobes; no event is alight at the middle (frame 3150) or at a handover. proof.cameraHeld: true holds the camera of the surface view at the pose of frame 3150 while time runs, for the life only sheet; false in the film.
